cards.front: What event triggered the outbreak of the First World War?
cards.back: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo, 28 June 1914
Gavrilo Princip, a Bosnian Serb linked to the Black Hand
Germany's plan to defeat France quickly by going through Belgium, then turn east to fight Russia

cards.front: Why did Britain enter the war in August 1914?
cards.back: Germany invaded neutral Belgium; Britain had guaranteed Belgian neutrality (Treaty of London 1839)

cards.front: What were the two alliance blocs before 1914?
cards.back: Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) and Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy)

cards.front: What was the significance of the Battle of the Marne (1914)?
cards.back: Halted the German advance on Paris; led to trench warfare on the Western Front

cards.front: What happened at the Battle of the Somme?
cards.back: 1916 British/French offensive; 57,000 British casualties on the first day; little ground gained
1916 German attempt to "bleed France white"; ~10 months long; symbol of French resistance
1915 Allied attempt to take the Dardanelles from the Ottoman Empire; failed with heavy ANZAC losses
German U-boats sinking all ships, including neutral ones, in the war zone around Britain
1917 German offer to Mexico of an alliance against the USA; helped bring the US into the war

cards.front: When did the USA enter the First World War?
cards.back: April 1917

cards.front: What was the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk?
cards.back: March 1918 peace between Bolshevik Russia and Germany; Russia lost huge territory
11 November 1918

cards.front: What was the War Guilt Clause?
cards.back: Article 231 of the Treaty of Versailles; Germany accepted responsibility for the war

cards.front: Name three terms of the Treaty of Versailles
cards.back: Reparations (£6.6bn), army limited to 100,000, loss of Alsace-Lorraine and colonies, demilitarised Rhineland
US President Wilson's peace aims: self-determination, open diplomacy, free trade, League of Nations

cards.front: What was the League of Nations?
cards.back: International body set up in 1920 after the war to keep peace; USA never joined

cards.front: What new weapons were used on the Western Front?
cards.back: Poison gas, tanks, machine guns, aircraft, heavy artillery
Stalemate; mud, rats, trench foot, shelling; no man's land between front lines

cards.front: When did the French Revolution begin?
What were the three Estates of the Ancien Régime?
cards.back: First Estate: clergy; Second Estate: nobility; Third Estate: everyone else (~97%)

cards.front: Why did Louis XVI call the Estates-General in 1789?
cards.back: France was bankrupt after wars (incl. American War of Independence) and needed new taxes

cards.front: What was the Tennis Court Oath?
cards.back: 20 June 1789: the Third Estate (now the National Assembly) swore not to separate until France had a constitution
Storming of the Bastille, a royal prison and symbol of royal tyranny

cards.front: What was the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen?
cards.back: August 1789 statement of liberty, equality before the law and popular sovereignty
Summer 1789 peasant panic and attacks on noble châteaux in the countryside

cards.front: What was the Flight to Varennes?
cards.back: June 1791: Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette tried to escape France and were caught; trust in the king collapsed
Radical revolutionary club led by Robespierre; dominated the Convention 1793-94
More moderate republicans; favoured war in 1792; purged by the Jacobins in 1793
21 January 1793, by guillotine

cards.front: What was the Reign of Terror?
cards.back: 1793-94: the Committee of Public Safety executed ~17,000 "enemies of the revolution"

cards.front: What was the Committee of Public Safety?
cards.back: Executive body of the Convention during the Terror, led by Robespierre

cards.front: What was the Law of Suspects?
cards.back: September 1793 law allowing arrest of anyone suspected of opposing the revolution
July 1794: Robespierre overthrown and executed; end of the Terror
Government of France 1795-99; five directors; weak and corrupt

cards.front: How did Napoleon come to power?
cards.back: Coup of 18 Brumaire (November 1799); became First Consul
Working-class Parisian radicals who wore trousers rather than knee breeches

cards.front: What was the Civil Constitution of the Clergy?
cards.back: 1790 law making priests state employees; split the Church and turned many Catholics against the revolution

cards.front: What was the Levée en masse?
cards.back: August 1793 mass conscription of all able-bodied men into the army

cards.front: When did the Cold War begin, roughly?
cards.back: After 1945; tensions clear by 1947 (Truman Doctrine)
1947 US promise to support free peoples resisting communism (Greece, Turkey); policy of containment
US economic aid to rebuild Western Europe after 1945 (~$13bn), to stop the spread of communism
1948-49 Soviet blockade of West Berlin; answered by the Berlin Airlift
1949: Western military alliance (USA, Britain, France and others)
1955 military alliance of the USSR and its Eastern European satellite states
Churchill's 1946 phrase for the division of Europe between the Soviet bloc and the West

cards.front: When was the Berlin Wall built and when did it fall?
cards.back: Built August 1961; fell November 1989

cards.front: What was the Cuban Missile Crisis?
cards.back: October 1962: 13-day standoff over Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba; Kennedy vs Khrushchev

cards.front: How was the Cuban Missile Crisis resolved?
cards.back: Khrushchev removed missiles from Cuba; USA promised not to invade Cuba and secretly removed missiles from Turkey
1956 revolt against Soviet control; crushed by Soviet tanks
1968 reforms by Dubček in Czechoslovakia; ended by Warsaw Pact invasion
Soviet right to intervene in any Warsaw Pact country where communism was threatened
Easing of Cold War tensions in the 1970s: SALT I, Helsinki Accords
1972 Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty limiting nuclear missiles
Competition between the USA and USSR to build more and better nuclear weapons
Mutually Assured Destruction: nuclear war would destroy both sides, so neither would start one

cards.front: Why did the USSR invade Afghanistan?
cards.back: 1979, to support the communist government; ended détente
Gorbachev's policies of openness and economic restructuring in the 1980s

cards.front: When did the Soviet Union collapse?
cards.back: December 1991
1950-53: communist North (backed by China, USSR) vs South (UN, USA); ended at the 38th parallel
US-Soviet competition in space: Sputnik 1957, Gagarin 1961, Moon landing 1969
